title: Ceiling on the Days of Cover of a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan Election
content:
The days of cover a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election may carry are held to a ceiling, and the ceiling
follows how long the vehicle is reserved for on the Keyturn Trip Booking beneath the election.

**Where the booking reserves 1400 hours or more**, the ceiling is 120 days.

**Where the booking reserves 360 hours or more but fewer than 1400 hours**, the ceiling is 90 days.

**Where the booking reserves fewer than 360 hours**, the ceiling is 30 days.

## Both sides of the two thresholds

| Reserved hours on the booking | Ceiling on the days of cover |
|---|---|
| 1399 | 90 days |
| 1400 | 120 days |
| 359 | 30 days |
| 360 | 90 days |

The thresholds are met at the figure itself: a booking reserving exactly 1400 hours stands at the upper
threshold and takes the 120-day ceiling, and a booking reserving exactly 360 hours stands at the lower
threshold and takes the 90-day ceiling. One hour short of either figure the booking takes the ceiling below.

## Hypothetical reservations read against the ceiling

A booking reserving 72 hours — a long weekend — falls under 360 hours and is held to 30 days. A booking
reserving 720 hours — about a month — falls between the two thresholds and is held to 90 days. A booking
reserving 2160 hours — about a quarter — stands above 1400 hours and is held to 120 days. In each case the
ceiling is a limit on what the election may carry, so an election whose days would otherwise come to more than
the ceiling carries the ceiling instead.
